# Web Agentic Memory

> Web Agentic Memory (WAM) is shared, verified memory for web-based workflows across websites and apps. AI agents retrieve short, task-specific hints for a public URL through MCP or the WAM CLI, then use their existing browser tools to carry out the work. Contributions are opt-in and require explicit consent.

WAM returns workflow hints; it does not install browser controls or act on the website. Public recall does not require a WAM account. Performance observations are one-off and do not promise a general speed improvement.

## Product

- [Website](https://webagenticmemory.com/): Product overview and current evidence.
- [Agent setup guide](https://webagenticmemory.com/guide): Configure MCP or CLI and make a first public recall.
- [Korean setup guide](https://webagenticmemory.com/ko/guide): Korean-language setup steps.
- [Public memory library](https://webagenticmemory.com/memories): Browse workflow examples and verified memories.
- [Contribution form](https://webagenticmemory.com/contribute): Submit a normalized workflow summary with consent.
- [Public benchmarks](https://webagenticmemory.com/#productivity-benchmarks): Current measured workflow comparisons and limitations.

## Accuracy notes

- Google Calendar and Canva have current live workflow comparisons; Medium and Naver results are earlier pilots, and editor-fixture results use a different protocol.
- Notion performance is pending remeasurement. Google Docs has a functional check but no paired timing; Google Flow, Google Slides, Gmail and Figma have workflow examples but no paired timing benchmark.
